title: Bringing trusted Fabric IQ context to wherever people and agents work
author: NelGson

content.text:
If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
Over the past year, AI has moved from answering questions to doing the work. As the 2026 Microsoft Work Trend Index shows, people are now handing entire tasks to agents and directing several at once. Those agents plan, decide, and act across systems, with less human review at every step.
Fabric IQ helps turn your organization's business knowledge into an advantage for people and agents. As agents take on more responsibility, that knowledge matters more than which model they run on. Every organization can use the same frontier models. What sets yours apart is its context layer: the definitions, metrics, relationships, and rules that describe how your business actually works. When you connect that context with knowledge from across the organization, people and agents can uncover insights and take informed action that reflects how the business operates.
The organizations seeing results treat business context as shared infrastructure, built once and reused by every agent.
Today at Microsoft Ignite 2026, we're extending the reach of Fabric IQ, the part of Microsoft IQ that captures how your business operates, to more of the places where that work happens, including Microsoft Copilot, Excel, ChatGPT and Codex by OpenAI, Claude by Anthropic, Fabric apps, and GitHub Copilot. We're also strengthening every foundation beneath it, from Microsoft OneLake and semantic models to ontologies and Fabric agents, so the context your teams define can power every agent that follows.
Fabric IQ and Microsoft IQ
A common challenge in getting agents into production is that the context, data, models, and runtime they depend on sit in silos, so teams end up rebuilding them for every project.
Microsoft IQ, which we're introducing today, is the enterprise context management platform that helps organizations build their own IQ by capturing, governing, and reusing the business knowledge their apps and agents depend on. It connects context from Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ, so every agent starts from what your organization already knows. New business plugins let teams package that knowledge into context, skills, and tools that colleagues across the business can trust and reuse.
Learn more in Yitzhak Kesselman and Tina Schuchman’s Microsoft IQ blog post.
Within Microsoft IQ, Fabric IQ models how your business operates. It powers a continuous loop where people and agents observe live signals, reason over shared context, and take governed action across analytics, operations, and the tools where work happens. It brings together three layers of business context and the agents that put it to work:
• Unified data: Microsoft OneLake brings analytical and operational data together in a single, accessible layer.
• Business intelligence: Power BI semantic models provide the governed metrics and definitions organizations already use to measure their business.
• Operational intelligence: Ontologies define business entities, their relationships, and the rules that govern them, so agents can reason in the language of the business. With live signals from Fabric Real-Time Intelligence, they also reflect what's happening right now.
Agents sit on top of these layers and put that context to work. Specialized agents add expertise of their own: Fabric data agents answer natural-language questions the way the teams who know the data best would, and operations agents monitor live data and recommend action when conditions change. Broader agents like Microsoft Copilot combine Fabric IQ with the rest of Microsoft IQ, such as emails, meetings, and documents, to complete work that spans the business.
Bring trusted business context to more experiences with Fabric IQ
The business questions people ask don't change based on where they ask them. With Fabric IQ, conversational analytics draws on the same business context wherever people and agents work. New integrations across Microsoft and third-party experiences carry the context your teams define once into more of the tools they use every day, so insights and actions rest on the same understanding of the business.
Grounding Microsoft Copilot in your business with data agents (General Availability) Coming Soon
Every day, millions of business users turn to Microsoft Copilot to find information, analyze data, and get work done. For many, it has become the first place they go to understand what's happening in the business. As people hand Copilot larger, multistep tasks, an answer that uses the wrong definition of revenue, or misses how a delay ripples through operations, can send a decision in the wrong direction.
Power BI semantic models in Microsoft Copilot are already generally available, so answers reflect the metrics your organization has agreed on. Next, we're bringing Fabric data agents to Microsoft Copilot, with general availability coming soon. Anyone in Copilot Chat or Cowork will be able to get specialist answers from agents your teams have configured by simply attaching a data agent. And with Work IQ, Copilot can combine this business context with the emails, meetings, and documents around a decision.
Figure: Animated GIF - In Microsoft Copilot Chat, a user attaches a Fabric data agent to a prompt and gets an answer grounded in the organization's business data, combined with context from Work IQ.
Bringing Fabric IQ to ChatGPT and Claude (Preview) Coming Soon
Many organizations use Microsoft Copilot alongside other AI assistants. That’s why we are introducing Fabric IQ plugins for ChatGPT and Claude, in preview coming soon, which bring insights from Power BI semantic models directly into both assistants. Users can ask questions of their enterprise data without opening a report, and answers draw on the measures your analysts already maintain, so a revenue figure in ChatGPT or Claude matches the one in your quarterly business review.
Figure: Animated GIF - In ChatGPT, a user connects the Fabric IQ plugin, asks it to find reports about inventory, and gets back the matching Power BI report.
Bringing Fabric IQ to Excel (Insiders Beta)
Excel is still where much of the business’s planning and forecasting happens, and with Copilot in Excel, more of those workbooks are now built through conversation. Figures exported from a report go stale quickly, though, and definitions drift each time they're copied. Currently available in Insiders Beta, this experience lets finance teams ask about revenue, margin, or variance in plain language. Copilot answers from governed Power BI semantic models and can build a live, Fabric-connected PivotTable to back it up. The numbers use the definitions the organization has already agreed on, and they stay current as the data refreshes.
Bringing Fabric IQ to Fabric apps (Generally Available) and GitHub Copilot (Preview)
A conversation is often where an insight starts, but a chat is hard to share and doesn't update when the data changes. Fabric apps let you carry those insights into apps that others can revisit, build on, and trust to stay current. Fabric apps are now generally available, and a new integration with Microsoft Copilot, in preview, lets people describe an app in natural language while Copilot builds it and sets up the Fabric resources behind it. Developers can also embed conversational experiences powered by Power BI semantic models and, coming soon, Fabric data agents into the apps they build with Fabric apps, in preview, turning insights from a single conversation into experiences teams use together.
We're also bringing ontologies in Fabric IQ to GitHub Copilot, in preview. As developers write code, GitHub Copilot can draw on the entities, relationships, and rules defined in your ontology, so the code it helps write reflects how your business works from the start.
Bringing Fabric IQ and Foundry IQ closer together (Generally Available)
Agents need two kinds of knowledge to get work right. Fabric IQ captures how the business operates through its data, metrics, and rules, while Foundry IQ brings in the institutional knowledge in documents, policies, and contracts. Foundry IQ can use Power BI semantic models from Fabric IQ, plus OneLake items, as knowledge sources. Agents built in Microsoft Foundry can draw on governed metrics alongside indexed documents, with OneLake permissions applied for each user.
Your data's protections come with it. With OneLake security, you can create roles that set permissions at the data item, folder, table, or even row and column level, so you can share a data item while restricting access to any sensitive data it contains. Those roles apply in Foundry IQ, so whether a user or an agent runs a search, results include only the data they're permitted to see.
We're also expanding what agents can learn from. Power BI semantic models from Fabric IQ, along with OneLake shortcuts and mirrored items, are now in preview as knowledge sources in Foundry IQ. Agents built in Microsoft Foundry can reason over the metrics your analysts maintain and over data connected from across your estate, without copying it into a separate store.
Partners are already building on Fabric and Foundry together to help their clients create transformational AI experiences. Brian Elliott, McKinsey Senior Partner and Co-Lead of EcliptOS, shared, "AI needs more than access to data. AI needs to understand how a business works. McKinsey’s EcliptOS platform brings together Microsoft Fabric IQ and Microsoft Foundry IQ to connect business data with enterprise knowledge. We build on that foundation with McKinsey’s industry expertise, codified into impact recipes, and our transformation capabilities to turn business context into persistent business value."
Learn about more of the innovation coming to Foundry IQ in the Foundry IQ blog.
Bringing Fabric IQ to any agent with Fabric IQ MCP and Skills for Fabric
Many of the agents your organization uses won't come from Microsoft. Fabric IQ MCP, now generally available, is a remote Model Context Protocol server that connects any compatible agent or app to Fabric IQ while respecting the permissions people already have in Fabric. Skills for Fabric is an open-source collection that teaches agents how to work with Fabric, from finding the right content to answering business questions. Together, they let you bring Fabric IQ to whichever agents your teams choose, so each one works from the same view of your business.
Strengthening each semantic layer of Fabric IQ
The semantic layer is one of an organization's most strategic assets. More than 22 million Power BI semantic models are in use every day, and the business meaning they hold increasingly grounds agents, apps, and Microsoft Copilot.
At Ignite, we're applying that approach to every layer of Fabric IQ, from metrics defined directly on data in OneLake and richer semantic models to ontologies that are faster to build and govern, and IQ sharing for teams, customers, and partners.
Defining business meaning where your data lives with semantic views (Preview)
Metrics such as revenue, margin, and active customers are often rebuilt in every tool that uses them, causing agents to inherit inconsistent definitions and potentially produce conflicting or unreliable insights. Semantic views (Preview), is a new capability that enables customers to define governed business metrics and semantics directly where their data lives in OneLake. By defining metrics once and reusing them across Fabric, organizations can standardize business definitions and ensure consistency. Built around the emerging Apache Ossie open standard, semantic views are designed for interoperability, enabling customers to extend and reuse semantic definitions across external data platforms and ecosystems, including Snowflake and other partners over time.
Figure: Semantic views provide governed business context across analytics, applications, and AI experiences.
Accelerate ontology creation and governance
Semantic models capture how the business is measured, and ontologies capture how it operates. An ontology defines the concepts your business runs on, such as customers, products, and shipments, along with their relationships, rules, and metrics. You can build one from scratch or have an agent create one from your existing Power BI semantic models. As more organizations put ontologies into production, they need them to cover more of the business, connect to more data, and meet enterprise security standards.
New updates, all in preview, address each:
• Ontology Health: Continuously checks an ontology for structural issues, missing configuration, and gaps in clarity and coverage. Results are labeled Critical, Warning, or Information, and guided actions take modelers straight to the element that needs attention.
Figure: Animated GIF - In Fabric IQ, Ontology Health lists the issues in an ontology by severity. A modeler opens one, reviews the proposed fix and what it would affect, applies it, and reruns the health check to confirm fewer errors and warnings.
• Customer-managed keys: Teams can protect ontology data and metadata at rest with their own encryption keys and rotate them under internal policies.
• Workspace outbound access protection: Outbound connections are blocked by default, so admins can allow only approved destinations and reduce the risk of data exfiltration.
• Richer modeling: Metrics, calculations, inheritance, and reuse let teams define a concept once and extend it across domains.
• More data sources: Ontologies connect to more OneLake data, including Eventhouse for real-time data, and to graph experiences for exploring how entities relate.
• Updated ontology skills: Skills for Fabric now includes updated ontology skills, so coding agents work with current capabilities.
Learn more about these ontology enhancements in the Fabric November 2026 Feature Summary.
Share data and business context more widely with IQ sharing (Preview)
Microsoft OneLake connects data across clouds, applications, and platforms through mirroring and shortcuts. IQ sharing extends that reach to business context, helping organizations securely share governed data and context with teams, customers, and partners. In addition to governed tables and files, markdown agent instructions, and RDF ontologies, IQ sharing now supports ontologies in Fabric IQ, coming soon to preview. Providers can share their business context without recipients recreating the underlying definitions, and recipients use shared semantic models and ontologies in Fabric IQ experiences while the provider keeps control.
Create and manage agents in Fabric
The value of a shared intelligence foundation comes when agents can use that context to deliver real outcomes. New enhancements across agents in Fabric make it easier to build, govern, and operationalize AI experiences across Microsoft Fabric and other AI platforms.
Make Fabric data agents faster, smarter, and easier to govern
Fabric data agents turn your data teams' expertise into agents anyone can ask questions of, in Fabric, Microsoft Copilot, and the apps your organization builds. As more people rely on them, users need fast, accurate answers, creators need easier ways to add context, and IT needs visibility and control. New updates address each:
• Faster, more accurate answers (Generally Available): Data agents respond with lower latency, return result sets larger than 25 rows, and understand time-relative questions such as "What were sales yesterday?" in the user's time zone.
• Better agents from existing knowledge (Preview): Query templates for SQL and semantic models answer common questions the same way every time, and instructions can be longer.
• Creators can configure Power BI semantic models directly in the data agent and import what they've defined in Prep data for AI.
• AI-assisted setup uses uploaded documentation and a semantic model's tables, measures, and query patterns to suggest instructions and example queries for creators to approve.
• Data agents can call Fabric user data functions as tools.
• Monitoring and governance (Preview): Data agent metrics appear in the Monitor hub, and Microsoft Foundry observability lets teams trace and evaluate data agents alongside other agents.
• Data agents register in Microsoft Agent 365 with an enterprise identity, so IT can govern them from the Microsoft 365 admin center.
• Creators can review user feedback to improve their data agents.
Learn more about these data agent enhancements in the Fabric November 2026 Feature Summary.
Get started with Fabric IQ
Learn more about Fabric IQ and read about every Fabric enhancement in the Fabric November 2026 Feature Summary.
